I have farmed these 9 mu in Quzhou for 20 years now. I am 49 years old and only finished primary school, but I know my own land. My son works off-farm in Handan city, so it is mostly me and my wife farming, with my daughter coming to help at busy times. We have a well, so water is there, but pumping costs electricity money, so I do not water for no reason.

Last year I planted 5 mu of cotton, 3 mu of maize, and 1 mu of mungbean. The cotton yield was just okay. I used the same traditional seed I always kept, but my neighbor Lao Wang across the ditch bought hybrid cotton seed from the input dealer, and his bolls were clearly bigger and the lint was whiter. I walked over to his field three times to look. So this year I will spend the extra money and buy that hybrid seed for my 5 mu of cotton. For maize, everyone around here uses hybrid now anyway — no one plants traditional maize anymore, the yield is too low. For the 1 mu of mungbean, I saved my own seed from last year, the small green kind. No need to buy seed for just 1 mu.

I think in bags, not in books. For cotton, I put one 50kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu at sowing time — the bag says 15-15-15. That never changes. Then I top-dress with urea twice, about 15 kg per mu each time, once when the flowers open and once when the bolls are setting. So about 30 kg of urea total per mu. I water three times from the well: once after sowing if the spring is dry, once at flowering, and once at boll stage. I spray pesticide seven times — cotton cannot survive without spray. The bollworm, aphids, and red spider mite will destroy everything if you skip even one spray. I rotary till before sowing.

For the 3 mu of summer maize, I sow after the early crop comes off in June. I put 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at sowing, then 20 kg of urea when the leaves are big and the plant is growing fast — the dealer calls it the trumpet stage. I water twice, once at sowing if the weather is dry, and once when the tassels come out. Three pesticide sprays: herbicide at sowing, then insecticide twice for armyworm and aphids.

The 1 mu of mungbean is the easiest. I spread about 15 kg of compound fertilizer per mu before sowing. Water twice, once when it sprouts and once when the pods are filling. Two sprays for insects. That is all.

I always calculate the cost in my head. A bag of compound fertilizer is over 150 yuan now, and urea is not cheap either. But I would rather put a little too much fertilizer than too little. If my cotton fails, I lose several thousand yuan. If I waste half a bag of fertilizer, I lose 80 yuan. The math is simple. I also watch what my neighbors do. If everyone around me applies one bag of compound per mu, I apply one bag per mu. I do not want to be different — change is risky. My budget is connected: if I spend more on fertilizer, I have less for hiring labor, but we do most work ourselves anyway.
